fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: After consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, Logan called for two more hikes and Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open. An AI-led stock rout has since erased half-point bets, and Bessent warned the Fed risks overtightening, so Warsh's committee weighs hikes into a correction with the Treasury leaning on it. This week's PCE reading lands first.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency convenes it after Trump's Shenzhen summit with Xi and Putin, billed as a nuclear summit, brought three of its leaders to one table, and after COP31 deadlocked over a fossil-fuel transition and finance for developing economies. What this summit settles is whether either thread reaches the wider group.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: One of the last meetings before Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February, it follows Paris and Berlin trading the succession: Spain takes the presidency, Germany the chief economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier. Meanwhile France's borrowing premium over Germany has hit 1.75 points, and the bank has so far left France to markets.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: UK inflation accelerated again in October and has now run above target for more than two years, which leaves the committee weighing a persistence that no longer reads as a one-off to look through. The decision settles whether the Bank of England answers a second run of acceleration or keeps waiting for prices to turn on their own.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, and Washington sold $500 million of euros for yen after it breached 160. Core inflation then came in at 2.2%, under the 2.3% forecast, so the board weighs a currency that is squeezing Takaichi's defence budget against prices that undershot.

fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-11-25.recent: The release lands days after reporting that US consumers are holding up against inflation going into the holiday season. Household spending is the largest part of the figure, so this estimate settles whether that resilience shows up in what the economy actually produced.

fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on US personal income and spending, which carries the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It sets the inflation read that rate expectations and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-pce-2026-11-25.recent: This release lands just before the holiday season, after reports that US consumers are holding up against inflation going into it. It settles whether that resilience shows in the spending figures themselves, and how fast the prices those households pay are still rising.

fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.recent: The release follows reports that US consumers are holding up against inflation going into the holiday season. Household spending is the largest share of US output, and this release settles how much of that resilience carried through to growth across the economy as a whole.
